newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares tumble on political uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares tumble on political uncertainty.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly lower on Tuesday as investors continued to express concern over allegations of government corruption, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares fell 2.95 percent, or 7.68 points, to 252.79 on low all-share turnover of 137 million shekels unchanged from Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 2.95 percent lower at 261.72.

"What we saw today was a violent correction in the wake of the political scandal. Since Sunday the mood in the market has changed as investors fear that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu might face criminal charges," said Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex Securities.

Netanyahu and other officials in his government are being questioned by police in connection with charges that the short-lived appointment of Roni Bar-On as attorney-general was part of a deal for a plea bargain in the corruption trial of Aryeh Deri, a key figure in the governing coalition.

"The probe has created a sense of unease but I believe that this is only a correction. The market was looking for a reason to consolidate and it came with the Bar-On story," said Izik Winish of Capital Securities.

"As long as the political uncertainty remains, the market will continue to be very volatile with a downside tendency. The rate reduction had no impact on trading today as investors focused on the corruption story," Nahum said.
After the closing of trading on Monday the Bank of Israel said it was lowering its key lending rate for March by 0.3 percentage point to an annualised 13.9 percent.
"The market is still very high and its sharp rise was crazy. In the long run the positive trend will continue but in the coming days trading will be very volatile," Winish added.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which fell 2.0 percent to 32,691 agorot on turnover of 9.1 million shekels; Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which lost 2.0 percent to 19,424 agorot on turnover of 9.0 million shekels; and Bank Hapoalim, which dropped 3.0 percent to 650 agorot on volume of 5.6 million shekels.
